subject: religious-studies
title: Arguments for God: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the classic arguments philosophers have given for the existence of God.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Arguments for God walkthrough — cosmological, teleological, ontological and moral arguments.
final_note: You learned the four main classical arguments and the key thinkers who shaped them.

concepts.def: Everything that exists has a cause — first cause is God
The universe shows design — designer is God
God's existence follows from God's perfect nature
Universal moral laws point to a divine lawgiver
Belief in a personal God who acts in the world
Belief that no God or gods exist

walkthroughs.body_html:
Two classic arguments start from the world around us.

The cosmological argument says everything that exists must have a cause. So there must be a First Cause — God. Aquinas set this out in his Five Ways.

The teleological argument says the universe shows complex design — like a watch needs a watchmaker (William Paley, 1802).

The ontological argument (Anselm) says God is 'that than which nothing greater can be thought' — so God must exist in reality as well as in the mind.

The moral argument says objective right and wrong need a divine source (C.S. Lewis argued this in 'Mere Christianity').

Atheists like David Hume challenged the design argument: bad design (disease, disasters) doesn't fit a perfect designer.

The problem of evil — if God is all-powerful and all-loving, why does suffering exist? — is the strongest classical objection.
